title: Urea 46% N Fertilizer
description: Prilled and granular urea (46-0-0) — the most concentrated solid nitrogen fertilizer, supplied to date palm, vegetable, and cereal growers across Oman.

details.longDescription:
Urea (CO(NH2)2, CAS 57-13-6) at 46% nitrogen is the most concentrated solid nitrogen fertilizer available and the main nitrogen source across Oman's agriculture: date palm plantations in Al Batinah and Al Dakhiliyah, vegetable farms, greenhouses and cereal and forage cropping. Global Chemicals LLC supplies standard fertilizer-grade prilled urea (1–2.4 mm) and granular urea (2–4 mm) from stock in Muscat in 25 kg PP bags and 1,000 kg big bags, with biuret below 1.0% and moisture below 0.5%.

Which form to order depends on how it is applied. Prilled urea dissolves fastest and suits fertigation through drip systems and foliar sprays; granular urea spreads evenly from broadcast spreaders and blends with other granular fertilizers without segregating. The biuret limit matters most for foliar use: biuret is phytotoxic to leaves, so a 0.5–1.0% foliar solution should be made only from low-biuret urea (biuret about 0.25% or less). Typical date palm programmes apply 150–300 kg of urea per hectare per season, split into several doses from late winter through fruit development rather than one heavy application.

In Oman's alkaline calcareous soils (pH 7.5–8.5), urea left on the surface hydrolyses to ammonium and loses a large share of its nitrogen as ammonia gas. Incorporate it or water it in the same day, or deliver it through fertigation, where the loss is small. In drip systems urea dissolves completely and endothermically, so the stock tank cools noticeably; mix in batches and let it reach ambient temperature before injection.

Urea is hygroscopic. Keep bags closed, off the floor and out of direct sun; once opened in humid coastal air it cakes within days. Do not dry-blend urea with calcium nitrate or ammonium nitrate: the mixture absorbs moisture and turns to slurry in storage. Beyond the farm, the same product is the feedstock for urea-formaldehyde and melamine resins; automotive-grade urea for diesel exhaust fluid is a different specification, so ask before ordering for that use.

faqs.answer: Yes, as a dilute solution of about 0.5–1.0%, but only from low-biuret urea (biuret about 0.25% or less), because biuret damages leaves. Standard fertilizer grade allows up to 1.0% biuret, so for foliar programmes tell us the use when you order and we will confirm the batch biuret on the certificate of analysis or offer a low-biuret lot. faqs.question: Is fertilizer urea the same as the urea used in AdBlue (diesel exhaust fluid)?

title: Diammonium Phosphate (DAP 18-46-0)
description: Granular DAP fertilizer — 18% nitrogen, 46% phosphate — the highest-analysis phosphorus fertilizer for base dressing across Omani farms.

details.longDescription:
Diammonium phosphate (DAP, (NH4)2HPO4, CAS 7783-28-0) is the 18-46-0 granular fertilizer that carries more phosphorus per tonne than any other common product: 18% nitrogen as ammonium and 46% P2O5, more than 90% of it water-soluble, in 2–4 mm granules. Global Chemicals LLC supplies it from stock in Muscat in 50 kg bags and 1,000 kg big bags to vegetable, alfalfa, cereal and date-palm growers across Oman, and as the phosphate component of custom NPK blends.

Where it fits. DAP is a base dressing: applied before planting or at establishment, it supplies the phosphorus that roots, tillering and early growth depend on, plus a starter dose of ammonium nitrogen. Typical base dressings run from 100 to 250 kg/ha for vegetables and cereals, set from the soil test; alfalfa and forage stands take it at establishment; mature date palms take about 1 kg per palm per year placed in the root zone. In Oman's calcareous soils phosphate is fixed by calcium within weeks of contact, so place DAP in a band near the roots or in the planting hole rather than broadcasting it on the surface, and keep it 5 cm or more from seed, because the ammonia released as the granule dissolves can injure germinating seedlings.

What it is not for. DAP solutions are alkaline and precipitate calcium phosphate in hard irrigation water, so it blocks drip emitters; use MAP or a water-soluble NPK for fertigation, and never put DAP in a stock tank with calcium nitrate or magnesium sulphate. For dry blending, its 2–4 mm granule matches granular urea and potassium chloride, so blends stay uniform in the bag and the spreader.

Storage and handling: DAP is not hazardous and not an oxidiser, but it is moderately hygroscopic, so keep bags closed, off the floor and shaded; wet DAP cakes and will not spread. A certificate of analysis giving nitrogen, total and water-soluble P2O5 and granule size comes with every lot, with a safety data sheet.

details.longDescription:
Muriate of Potash (MOP / potassium chloride, 60% K2O) is the most widely used potassium fertilizer in Oman — critical for date palm fruit sizing, quality, and post-harvest storage life, and for tolerance to Oman's saline groundwater. title: Calcium Nitrate Fertilizer
description: Water-soluble calcium nitrate — 15.5% N, 26.5% CaO — the standard calcium and nitrate-nitrogen source for fertigation of tomatoes, cucumbers, and greenhouse crops.

details.longDescription:
Fertilizer-grade calcium nitrate (calcium ammonium nitrate decahydrate, 5Ca(NO3)2·NH4NO3·10H2O, CAS 15245-12-2) is the water-soluble fertilizer that delivers calcium and nitrate nitrogen together: 15.5% N (14.4% nitrate, 1.1% ammonium) and 26.5% CaO, dissolving at 1,290 g/L at 20 °C with insolubles below 0.05%, so it leaves no residue in tanks, filters or drip emitters. Global Chemicals LLC supplies it from stock in Muscat in 25 kg bags and 1,000 kg big bags for greenhouse and open-field growers in Nizwa, Barka and across Al Batinah.

It is the standard calcium source for fertigation and hydroponics across Oman because it is the only common calcium fertilizer that is fully soluble and because nitrate nitrogen is taken up directly and does not acidify or volatilise in the high-pH substrates and calcareous soils of the Sultanate. Calcium builds cell walls, so a steady supply prevents blossom-end rot in tomatoes, peppers and cucumbers, tip-burn in lettuce and brassicas, and bitter pit and cracking in fruit; calcium moves only with the transpiration stream, so it must be supplied continuously through the season rather than in one dose. Typical nutrient solutions carry 100–200 mg/L of calcium, which the grower sets from the water analysis; a foliar spray of 0.5–1% calcium nitrate in the early morning or evening supports fruit quality during heat.

Tank rules. Calcium nitrate goes in its own stock tank, the A tank of a two-tank fertigation system. Concentrated with phosphates it forms insoluble calcium phosphate, and with sulphates it forms gypsum, either of which blocks emitters; inject the A and B tanks separately and let them meet only in the dilute irrigation line. It can be blended with potassium nitrate, magnesium nitrate and chelated micronutrients.

Storage: the product is hygroscopic and will liquefy in humid coastal air, so keep bags sealed and indoors; it is an oxidiser, so store it away from fuels, oils and organic material. A certificate of analysis and safety data sheet come with every lot. title: Zinc Sulphate Monohydrate (33% Zn) — Agricultural
description: Micronutrient zinc sulphate — 33% Zn monohydrate — for correcting zinc deficiency in Oman's alkaline soils, date palm, and greenhouse crops.

details.longDescription:
Zinc sulphate monohydrate (ZnSO4·H2O, CAS 7446-19-7) at 33% zinc and 15% sulphur is the agricultural micronutrient that corrects the most widespread deficiency in Oman's soils. Global Chemicals LLC supplies it from stock in Muscat in 25 kg bags as a fully soluble, free-flowing powder or granule to date-palm, citrus, mango, vegetable, greenhouse and forage growers across the Sultanate; the fertilizers supplier guide linked on this page lists the companion products, and the heptahydrate and industrial grades are under inorganic chemicals.

Why zinc is short here. Oman's calcareous soils sit at pH 7.5–8.5 with little organic matter, and at that pH most of the soil's zinc is locked up out of reach of roots; sandy soils and heavy phosphate use make it worse. The symptoms are small, narrow, mottled leaves, short internodes, rosetting on fruit trees, and poor fruit set and size on date palm, citrus and mango; on vegetables and wheat, stunted plants and yield loss. A leaf or soil test confirms it before treatment and again before a repeat.

How to apply it. Soil: broadcast or band about 5–10 kg of zinc per hectare, which is 15–30 kg/ha of the monohydrate, before planting or at the start of the season, worked in or watered in, which lasts two to three seasons; do not tank-mix or place it with phosphate fertilizers, which precipitate zinc phosphate. Foliar: a 0.2–0.5% spray with a wetting agent, applied in the early morning or evening to avoid scorch, acts within days and is the quickest fix on an established crop. Fertigation: it dissolves cleanly and can be injected with other sulphate and nitrate fertilizers, never with the phosphate or calcium stock tank. Seed treatment coats cereal seed for early vigour. On very high-pH soils part of a soil application is fixed within weeks, so foliar sprays or chelated zinc EDTA, also available from us, are used alongside it.

Storage and handling: keep bags closed and dry; the product is harmful if swallowed, irritates eyes and is toxic to aquatic life, so keep spills out of drains and falaj channels and wear gloves and goggles when mixing. Every lot carries a certificate of analysis giving zinc and sulphur content and a safety data sheet.

title: Agricultural Gypsum (Calcium Sulphate)
description: Agricultural-grade gypsum (calcium sulphate dihydrate) for sodic soil reclamation, calcium supply, and structure improvement across Oman's irrigated farmland.

details.longDescription:
Agricultural gypsum is calcium sulphate dihydrate (CaSO4·2H2O, CAS 10101-41-4), mined and ground to below 2 mm, with 85% minimum purity; pure gypsum carries 23.3% calcium and 18.6% sulphur, so the product delivers at least about 20% calcium and 16% sulphur. It is the standard amendment for reclaiming sodic and saline-sodic soils across Oman's irrigated regions, where saline groundwater raises exchangeable sodium, disperses clay and destroys soil structure and infiltration. Gypsum supplies soluble calcium that displaces sodium from the cation exchange complex, so the soil re-aggregates and water moves through it again. It is also a non-acidifying calcium and sulphur source for peanuts, alfalfa and forage crops. Global Chemicals LLC supplies it from stock in Muscat in 25 kg bags, 1,000 kg big bags and bulk.

How much to apply. The dose depends on the exchangeable sodium percentage and the cation exchange capacity, which only a soil test gives; a working rule is about 1.7 tonnes of pure gypsum (about 2 tonnes of this 85% product) per hectare for every milliequivalent of exchangeable sodium per 100 g of soil to be replaced in the top 15 cm, which is why field rates run from 2 to 10 t/ha. Gypsum dissolves slowly (roughly 2.5 g/L), so the fine grind matters: finer particles react faster. Reclamation only works if the displaced sodium is leached out, so spread the gypsum before an irrigation that drains below the root zone and plan follow-up leaching with the best-quality water available.

Gypsum can also be dissolved in irrigation water to raise its calcium and lower its sodium adsorption ratio before it reaches the soil, which protects infiltration on drip and sprinkler schemes fed from brackish wells. Because it does not change soil pH and does not burn foliage, it can be applied to standing date palm, vegetables and forage without a withdrawal period, and it can be blended with most fertilizers except those that react with calcium, such as phosphates.

Store bags dry; the product is not hazardous and needs no special handling beyond dust control. title: Humic Acid (Leonardite Extract)
description: Water-soluble humic and fulvic acids — leonardite-derived soil conditioner that improves nutrient uptake, soil structure, and root growth in Oman's low-organic desert soils.

details.longDescription:
Humic acid (leonardite-derived potassium humate) is a powerful soil conditioner for Oman's low-organic-matter desert and irrigated soils. Boosts cation exchange capacity, chelates and mobilises phosphorus and micronutrients (particularly Fe and Zn), improves soil aggregate structure, and stimulates root growth. Compatible with drip fertigation and foliar sprays. Global Chemicals LLC supplies water-soluble flake and powder forms (65–75% humic acid) — ideal for regenerative fertilization programs on date palm, vegetables, and turf.

Dissolve humic acid in water before adding other fertilizers. It can flocculate in acidic solutions and in very hard water, so do not premix it with acids or concentrated calcium, and run a small jar test with your own irrigation water before filling the tank. In drip programmes it works best in small, frequent doses through the season rather than one large application, alongside a normal NPK programme rather than replacing it.
